accepted.question_text: Let k be a positive definite kernel on a compact domain X subset R^d, let H_k be the associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space, and suppose an unknown reward function f belongs to H_k with ||f||_{H_k} <= B. In the online setting, a learner sequentially chooses points x_1, x_2, ... in X, observes noisy rewards y_i = f(x_i) + epsilon_i with i.i.d. sub-Gaussian noise, and may choose each new point using all previous observations. If mu_n(x) and sigma_n(x) are the surrogate Gaussian-process posterior mean and standard deviation after n observations, what is the smallest possible growth rate in n of a confidence-width factor rho_n(delta) for which, with probability at least 1 - delta, the uniform bound |f(x) - mu_n(x)| <= rho_n(delta) sigma_n(x) holds for all x in X? In particular, can the existing online RKHS confidence interval be improved by an O~(sqrt(gamma_n)) factor, where gamma_n is the maximal information gain?

evidence.quote: In online learning problems, the observation points are collected sequentially. In particular, the observation point x_{i+1} is determined after all the values {(x_j , y_j )}^i_{j=1} are revealed.

Our open problem is concerned with improving this confidence interval. Open Problem. Under Assumption 1, in the online setting, consider the general problem of proving a confidence interval of the following form uniformly in x in X: |f(x) - mu_n(x)| <= rho_n(delta) sigma_n(x), with probability at least 1 - delta. What is the lowest growth rate of rho_n(delta) with n? In particular, is it possible to reduce the confidence interval width in Theorem 2 by an O~(sqrt(gamma_n)) factor?

accepted.question_text: In the same kernelized bandit setting with an unknown function f in an RKHS and maximal information gain gamma_N, can the standard GP-UCB algorithm, or a simple variation of it that still relies on a standard online confidence bound, achieve regret O~(sqrt(N gamma_N)) on compact domains instead of the currently derived O~(gamma_N sqrt(N)) bound?
accepted.context_brief: Whether GP-UCB can attain tight regret

evidence.quote: Following standard UCB-based bandit algorithm techniques, it can be shown that the GP-UCB algorithm (namely, repeatedly choosing x to maximize the current upper confidence bound) attains R(N) = O~(rho_N(delta) sqrt(N gamma_N)), with probability at least 1 - delta. Substituting rho_N(delta) from Theorem 2, we have R(N) = O~(gamma_N sqrt(N)).

In view of this discussion, the improvement from O~(gamma_N sqrt(N)) to O~(sqrt(N gamma_N)) has now been obtained using several different algorithms, but it remains to determine whether GP-UCB (or a simple variation thereof) can achieve it.
